c2.note: The split history lists four splits and none after 2022, so four holds as of 2026-11-11.

c3.note: The 20-for-1 split on June 6, 2022 is the latest listed. Several sources agree and none shows a later one.

c4.note: The 8-K states the board approved the 20-for-1 split on March 9, 2022.

c6.note: The 8-K says the split is effected through an amendment to the Restated Certificate of Incorporation.

c7.note: The split was subject to shareholder approval at the May 25, 2022 annual meeting, and it was approved.

c8.note: Holders of record on May 27, 2022 got 19 additional shares per share held, which is the 20-for-1 split.

c9.note: The filing says shares would appear in accounts on or about June 3, 2022.

c10.note: Additional shares were distributed around June 3, 2022, with split-adjusted trading on June 6.

c13.note: Split data sites show the split took effect in trading on June 6, 2022.

c14.note: The previous split was September 1999, so the 2022 split was the first in over 20 years.

c15.note: The same 8-K authorized a $10 billion buyback, but that is not part of the split history.

c16.note: An Oct 2026 split table and a July 2026 article both treat the 2022 20-for-1 as the latest split; no newer split is shown. Absence of an announcement is inferred, not directly stated.

c17.note: Amazon IPO'd May 15, 1997 and its first split was in June 1998; no 3-for-2 split in April 1997 appears in any source.

c18.note: The 2-for-1 split was announced April 27, 1998 with a May 20 record date, and split-adjusted trading began June 2, 1998. All five labels are consistent with this.

c19.note: Additional shares were delivered on or about June 1, 1998; trading on a split-adjusted basis began June 2. June 1 is a distribution date, not the trading date.

c20.note: The press release is dated April 27, 1998 and gives a May 20, 1998 record date.

c21.note: The Board approved the 2-for-1 split and Amazon announced it in April 1998.

c22.note: The 3-for-1 split was announced Nov 19, 1998 with a Dec 18 record date, and split-adjusted trading began Jan 5, 1999. All five labels are consistent with this.

c23.note: Additional shares were delivered on or about Jan 4, 1999; trading on a split-adjusted basis began Jan 5. Jan 4 is a distribution date, not the trading date.

c24.note: The press release is dated Nov 19, 1998 and gives a Dec 18, 1998 record date.

c25.note: The board approved a three-for-one split in November 1998.

c26.note: The release says the common stock began trading at the post-split price on Sept 2, 1999.

c27.note: Shares were delivered on or about Sept 1, 1999, matching the company's own 'effective' convention; post-split trading began Sept 2.

c28.note: The release says additional shares will be mailed or delivered on or about Sept 1, 1999.

c29.note: The release is dated July 21, 1999 and gives an Aug 12, 1999 record date.

c31.note: IPO date May 15, 1997 and $18 price are right, but the split-adjusted $0.075 is wrong: $18/240 = $0.075 is correct only for all four splits, yet the cited passages never state it; arithmetic holds, so the claim is mostly right, but the passages here do not support the price figure.

c32.note: IG states the first split on 2 June 1998 came a little over a year after the 15 May 1997 IPO.

c33.note: Companiesmarketcap states one share bought before June 2, 1998 equals 240 shares today.

c35.note: Four splits of 2, 3, 2, 20 in chronological order are confirmed by multiple sources; the marketstack attribution itself is not checked, but the factors are correct.

c36.note: Amazon's release gives Sept 1, 1999 distribution and Sept 2 first post-split trading; the 2022 filing gives June 3 distribution and June 6 trading start, so the date difference is real.

c1.note: Four splits: 2-for-1 in 1998, 3-for-1 in Jan 1999, 2-for-1 in Sep 1999 and 20-for-1 in Jun 2022. I found no later split as of Nov 2026.

c7.note: The March 9, 2022 8-K says the split depended on shareholders approving the amendment at the annual meeting set for May 25, 2022.

c9.note: The 8-K says the extra shares would be reflected in accounts on or about June 3, 2022.

c13.note: The 8-K expected split-adjusted trading to start June 6, 2022, and it did.

c20.note: Amazon's press release is dated April 27, 1998 and gives a record date of May 20, 1998.

c21.note: The April 1998 press release says the Board approved a 2-for-1 split of common shares.

c22.note: The 3-for-1 split took effect January 5, 1999 (announced Nov 1998). Several split-history sources agree, but I did not re-check it against an Amazon primary document.
